framing.lineOfInquiry: Ravi Arora (P00049) may have been involved in the incident recorded in CASE002
framing.alternate: Ravi Arora (P00049) was not involved — the evidence has an innocent explanation
framing.note: KRONOS starts from the presumption of innocence. The line of inquiry and the alternates are tested against the same records; neither is a finding, and the strengths are not probabilities.

alternateHypotheses.title: The contact was routine, not coordination
alternateHypotheses.statement: Ravi Arora's calls and messages reflect a long-standing relationship (family, work, business), not planning of the incident.
alternateHypotheses.label: Weak

evidence.text: In contact with Sachin Bansal since 2025-01-01, 22 days before the incident (5 calls, 3 messages) — a long-standing relationship
In contact with Vivek Arora since 2025-01-03, 21 days before the incident (14 calls, 13 messages) — a long-standing relationship

alternateHypotheses.test: Examine message content and the timing of contact relative to the incident; establish the relationship.

alternateHypotheses.title: Was near the scene for a routine reason
alternateHypotheses.statement: Ravi Arora was near the scene because they regularly go there (home, work, market), not because of the incident.
alternateHypotheses.label: Weak

evidence.text: Recorded within 1 km of the scene on 29 other days (01 Jan – 22 Feb), so presence there is part of their routine

alternateHypotheses.test: Establish why the person is regularly there (address, employment, shop) and compare the incident-time visit with their usual pattern (time of day, duration).

alternateHypotheses.title: Named or given a role in error
alternateHypotheses.statement: Ravi Arora was named in the FIR, or assigned a role, without an independent basis.
alternateHypotheses.label: Weak

evidence.text: Recorded in the FIR as victim, not as accused

alternateHypotheses.test: Re-examine the FIR and statements; record the person's statement and the informant's basis for naming them.

alternateHypotheses.title: The location records are unreliable
alternateHypotheses.statement: Ravi Arora's location records are imprecise or inconsistent (tower-level accuracy, cloned or shared SIM), so they do not reliably place them at the scene.
alternateHypotheses.label: Weak

evidence.text: Location inconsistency (requires air travel): IGI Airport Terminal 3, Delhi → Mumbai Airport Terminal 2, 1135.93 km in 145.0 min
Location inconsistency (impossible): Sector 17 Plaza, Chandigarh → Bandra West Residential, Mumbai, 1358.43 km in 60.0 min
Location inconsistency (requires air travel): Bandra West Residential, Mumbai → Sector 17 Plaza, Chandigarh, 1359.16 km in 116.4 min

alternateHypotheses.test: Request a tower dump and the handset's GPS logs; check for SIM cloning; rely on high-accuracy fixes only.

alternateHypotheses.title: The money has a legitimate explanation
alternateHypotheses.statement: The flagged money movements of Ravi Arora have an ordinary purpose (salary, rent, property, business) or belong to a co-holder of the account.
alternateHypotheses.label: Weak

evidence.text: Flagged UPI ₹6,983 on 2025-02-11 11:50 has a stated purpose 'loan repayment'

alternateHypotheses.test: Obtain full statements, invoices or agreements and KYC; confirm the stated purpose with the counter-party.

alternatesConsideredNotSupported.title: Someone else used the phone or handset

comparison.verdict: Every supporting item could be explained by at least one alternate, although the line of inquiry is stronger on weight (0.73 vs 0.29). Test the alternates before relying on it.
settleWith: A5 — Examine message content and the timing of contact relative to the incident; establish the relationship.

A6 — Re-examine the FIR and statements; record the person's statement and the informant's basis for naming them.

confidence.note: Evidential balance compares weighted supporting vs contradicting evidence; it is not a probability of guilt. Prior records are excluded from this score.

note: Each hypothesis is tested from both sides to reduce confirmation bias. Confidence scores are evidential balance (not probability of guilt). Human review is required.
